headline: Bullish on Bitcoin despite rising global bond yields; sees asymmetric upside as smart money identifies undervaluation after 9–12 month bear market
reasoning: James Ryan argues that Bitcoin has shown remarkable resilience and maturity, holding above key support levels even as the US 10-year yield hits 5.2% and Australian 10-year yields approach 5.3%, heading toward June 2008 highs of 6.5%. He notes Bitcoin made a low at $57.7K US and has since recovered strongly, which he attributes to institutional ETF inflows picking up and sustaining. He believes smart money recognised Bitcoin as undervalued during the June–August sideways period while retail investors were waiting for sub-$50K. Ryan sees the trend shifting in favour of bulls, with a near-term target of mid-to-high $90K US and a view that once the $100K psychological barrier is broken, further upside accelerates. He also draws a parallel to COVID-era monetary expansion, arguing that currency debasement trends since COVID structurally favour Bitcoin.
quote: It's absolutely defying those headwinds. It's quite amazing to see the resilience and the maturity of Bitcoin as an asset over the last couple of years really have the opportunity to stick around and have some nice smoothing volatility over the last couple of months despite the macro headwinds. So like right now we're seeing the yields across the board in all countries, not just Western countries really skyrocket. The US 10 years just hit 5.2%. The Aussie yields are 5.3 for the 10 year here and it's looking like it's heading towards the June 2008 highs at 6.5%. So the fact that Bitcoin has managed to hold with quite a lot of strength over the last few weeks after making a low at 57.7K US. It's amazing to see that it's actually getting a lot of that asymmetric upside opportunity and smart money investors are identifying the fact that Bitcoin has been undervalued the last 9 to 12 months in its bear market.
episode_title: Bitcoin defies bond yield surge as momentum builds

headline: Bitcoin primed to rally as bond yields cool, riding the next currency expansion cycle
reasoning: James Ryan argues that Bitcoin is well-positioned to benefit from the next easing cycle or from bond yields peaking and cooling off. He draws on the historical precedent of Bitcoin rallying from $10,000 to $69,000 in roughly six months during the last rate easing cycle, noting it became overvalued and corrected before the next expansion. He believes risk-on assets including Bitcoin will see rapid inflows once yields pull back, and that Bitcoin dominance tends to remain strong through the first two years of a bull market expansion.
quote: Bitcoin price action here is really primed to take advantage of that next expansion of currency. Or if even if it's the yields having to give some give some leeway if they do continue higher and then cool off. I think Bitcoin is really, really primed at that point to take advantage of that. And just like many risk on assets would be once, once the yields do cool down, I think people will be very quick to jump on the bandwagon again.
episode_title: Bitcoin defies bond yield surge as momentum builds
